task: blind reproduction of the M444 SOC-standardized apparent KE recovery. Definition: analyses/M444_spec.md Rev 2.1 (sections 1-4 and 11) and, for the interval definitions that feed it, analyses/M441_spec.md sections 1, 2, 9, 10, 11 (native v2 layer: consecutive native speed samples, episodes, plateau trimming, 0.05 s slices, assumed class masses 1890 kg urban/mixed; compute_summary_arrays._mass_for_drive for the others; SOC at the interval START from the BMS SoC channel; pack temperature = mean of the 4 probes at the interval start, M441 age rules). Do NOT read tools/*.py, tests/, analyses/M444_result.json, analyses/M44*/ or any other file under analyses/ except the three specs and this brief; you may reuse your own earlier code under analyses/M441_audit/ and analyses/M442_audit/ ONLY IF you wrote it (the M441 audit extractor was written from the spec text by an independent auditor and is allowed). Data: raw_only/<file>, drive_master.csv, seasonal_drive_master.csv (cohorts).
cohort: all (578 drives); day set = calendar days (master start date) with at least one kept interval (113 days); bootstrap: numpy default_rng(42).integers(0, D, (4000, D)) over the sorted days, counts per day, ratios recomputed in every draw with the weights held fixed.
tolerances: weights and coverage 1e-4; standardized and observed values 0.05 pp; intervals 0.15 pp; retained-band lists and dropped groups exact. Support floors: >= 200 strict-drop intervals, >= 10 drives, >= 5 days per joint cell (group x SOC band); the SOC band edges are 40/50/55/60/63/66/69/72/100 (lower-inclusive; below 40 explicit).
also_check: the common-support rule of spec section 3 and the drop order (applied to the speed view: which groups are dropped and why)
the single renormalization over the retained bands and that the weights are the same for both views
the language of the spec: anything ambiguous that you had to guess
return: JSON brief <2 KB to analyses/M444_audit.json (encoding='utf-8' on every text open): per item agree / differ with max differences, ambiguities, concerns. Write your own code under analyses/M444_audit/ (avoid Windows reserved file names such as con.py).
